question.text: A particle is projected vertically upwards with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>16</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, after some time, when it again passes through the point of projection, its speed is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. It is known that the work done by air resistance is the same during upward and downward motion. Then the maximum height attained by the particle is (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>) :

options.text: 8 m

solution.text:
From work-energy theorem 
For upward motion 1 2 m 1 6 2 = mgh + W  (work by air resistance)
For downward motion 1 2 m 8 2 = mgh - W ⇒ 1 2 1 6 2 + 8 2 = 2 gh  

or h=8 m
